title: Time-Based Key-Value Store
statement:
Design a key-value store that remembers every value a key has had, each with the time it was set, so you can ask what a key held at any moment. Write a `TimeMap` class with two operations:

- `set key value time` stores `value` for `key` at time `time`.
- `get key time` returns what `key` held at time `time`: the value set at the latest time that is at or before `time`. It returns `null` when `key` has no value set at or before `time`, which includes a key that was never set.

The first line is the count `q`. Each of the next `q` lines is one operation. Print the answer to each `get` on its own line. Keys and values are single words, and times are whole numbers from 1 to 1000000000. The times of the `set` operations only go up, so each key's values arrive in time order. One key can collect a great many values, so `get` should find its answer without looking at every one of them.

Input:

```text
7
set foo bar 1
get foo 1
get foo 3
set foo baz 4
get foo 4
get foo 2
get bar 5
```

Expected output:

```text
bar
bar
baz
bar
null
```

hints: Read `set` first. Each key keeps its own list of entries, and because times only go up, every list is already sorted by time.
In a sorted list you can binary search for the first entry set after `time`. The answer is the entry just before it, and there's none when that first entry is at the very start.
Python's `bisect_right`, C++'s `upper_bound`, and Go's `sort.Search` find that position for you. In JavaScript, TypeScript, and Java, write the binary search with a `lo` and a `hi`.
